title: Common counts of a society (social Lines)
description: Each entry is a Line as a plain count of a society: how many of a thing there are, reaching from 0. Where /5's math Lines are EXACT integers, these social counts are OBSERVED — published tallies for a stated period. A count is a Line laid unit by unit.

provenance.primary_source: US primary sources: US Census Bureau, US Senate/House, US Code, National Archives
provenance.note: Counts are OBSERVED published figures. Structural counts (states, senators) are stable by law; population counts carry a stated period. Counts are alphabetized by name for reader ease.
